headline: High: shared workspace plus broad outbound upload path creates default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no documented direct message channel, but A shares workspace state across instances and can ingest workspace pages; B operates on files and account data. That makes manual copy/paste or shared-content injection plausible, though not default. The pathway is weaker than shared-automation cases, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-generated text into a Notion page that A later summarizes or rewrites.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace content without provenance labeling.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to any B output before pasting into A.
Keep B outputs in a separate folder from A-ingested workspace pages.
Require human review before A acts on any B-authored text.
Use a dedicated staging page for cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while B has broad network egress and handles account data plus media files. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive workspace content into B’s outbound uploads or logs in default workflows. The blast radius includes multiple work products, so medium fits.
conditions: IF workspace pages from A are exported or copied into B for posting.
IF B uploads media or metadata derived from A’s knowledge-base content to external services.
mitigations: Do not route workspace pages into B unless redacted.
Disable or restrict B uploads for any content sourced from A.
Use a scrubber to remove names, IDs, and internal links before transfer.
Keep A and B on separate accounts/workspaces where possible.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem or modify git state, so classic destructive write conflicts are absent. The only overlap is shared workspace/account data handling, which can still cause coordination mistakes but not the high-severity same-dir write conflict described in the rubric. Low is sufficient.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external account or workspace resource.
IF the operator treats one agent’s edits as automatically synchronized with the other.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces/accounts to each agent.
Use a single human gate for any shared-resource update.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same account file or page set.
Document which agent owns each mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and B is a CLI uploader that can act on files and account data. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect uploads or posts. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text, captions, or summaries without independent verification.
IF A’s workspace-grounded answer is treated as a final source of truth for B’s posting workflow.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source files before upload.
Insert a human approval step between A and B.
Limit A to drafting only, not final factual claims.
Log source-to-output mappings for every cross-agent handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: A is vendor-hosted and sends data to Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers, while B has broad network egress and handles account data. For workspace content that includes regulated or residency-sensitive data, the pair can create retention and transfer mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium—not high—is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-sensitive content is stored in A’s workspace pages.
IF B transmits that content or derived metadata to external social platforms or services.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from A’s workspace pages.
Use a data-classification checklist before any B upload.
Confirm retention settings for both services before use.
Keep a deletion/export log for cross-posted content.
